description: Counterparty promises guaranteed high returns on a 'trading platform' and asks for an initial USDT deposit to 'unlock' further profits.
Someone claiming to be exchange/wallet support asks the user to 'verify' funds by sending USDT to a 'safe' address.
'Recovery agent' claims they can retrieve previously lost/stolen crypto in exchange for an upfront USDT fee.
Long-distance romantic contact suddenly needs an urgent USDT transfer for an emergency, customs fee, or travel cost.
heuristics: can't talk right now just send

description: Screenshot or link to a dashboard showing fabricated profits, asking for a deposit to withdraw the (nonexistent) balance.
Generic social-engineering pressure tactics that precede many of the categories above: urgency, secrecy, and discouraging the user from verifying independently.
A destination address that closely resembles (same first/last characters as) an address the user has sent to before, planted via a zero-value transfer to poison the recipient's history/autocomplete.

A 'job' offering commission for simple tasks (liking videos, submitting reviews, boosting app rankings) run through Telegram/WhatsApp, where early small payouts build trust before the platform demands a USDT deposit to 'unlock' bigger batches or withdraw earnings.

Someone posing as police, a prosecutor, or a tax/customs official claims the user's funds are linked to a crime or under investigation and must be moved to a 'safe' or 'supervised' USDT wallet to be cleared.
heuristics: transfer to a safe wallet for verification

description: A message claims the user was selected for a free token airdrop or giveaway, but must first send a small amount of USDT to cover a 'gas', 'activation', or 'unlock' fee before the (nonexistent) reward is released.
heuristics: you have been selected for an airdrop

description: A counterparty in a peer-to-peer/OTC USDT trade insists the buyer send funds first, or introduces a fake 'escrow' or 'middleman' account that disappears once payment lands.
heuristics: escrow bot will hold the funds

description: A link asks the user to 'reconnect', 'revalidate', or 'sync' their wallet on a fake dApp/exchange page that actually requests an unlimited USDT spending approval, letting the attacker drain the wallet afterward.
heuristics: your wallet needs to be revalidated
